entries.title: Review: Jae Stephens deserves a larger stage — and more hearts to break — in Lollapalooza debut
entries.summary: <p>Jae Stephens makes music for heartbreakers.</p><p>That much was true for the Los Angeles-based pop and R&B singer during her Lollapalooza debut Saturday on the BMI stage, where she sang odes to keeping a roster of men for options — and loving and leaving without regard.</p><p>“Which one should I choose today? Switch ’em out like shoes today,” she sang on her single “SMH,” with a sly smile to the delight of the crowd, who erupted when Stephens brought out Chicago’s very own Shea Couleé to snap into fierce choreography alongside her.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-5d0000" class="Figure-credit"><p>Giacomo Cain/For the Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Songs like “Him&Him&Him” had a bubbly lightness reminiscent of SWV’s 1998 classic “So Into You,” though Stephens’ was a little less tender — “I never save their numbers, just here for the summer,” she sang while popping on stage. And her song “Precious” had a bounce that conjured images of Ciara.</p><p>In response to the loud cheers for her, Stephens appeared to get emotional onstage, before clicking back into stunt mode.</p><p>Stephens and two backup dancers hit their marks, dedicating choreo to each song while Stephens kept singing without a hint of sounding winded, as if she trained at the Destiny’s Child academy for pop’s next big star.</p><p>In reality, Stephens, 29, has cut her teeth in the music industry and as a performer, releasing several mixtapes and writing songs for the likes of Jennifer Lopez.</p><p>Clocking in at just 30 minutes, Stephens felt deserving of a larger stage, longer set time and more hearts to break.</p>

entries.title: Review: Tate McRae closes out Lollapalooza with surprisingly subdued set
entries.summary: <p>Several songs into her headlining Lollapalooza set on Sunday night, Tate McRae pulled out a microphone stand to sing “Anything But Love,” as if to reiterate that she does, in fact, sing live in addition to performing high-energy choreography.</p><p>By no means a vocal dynamo, McRae is a competent singer, though audiences shouldn’t expect any vocal surprises. But the mic served as a symbol not of vocal prowess but an invitation to focus on McRae as a lyricist.</p><p>To her fans, she is not a manufactured pop star. Many of them have grown up with her since she began posting songs online as a teenager and resonate deeply with her lyrics, which often touch on heartbreak. They were likely happy with the set, which was surprisingly more subdued than expected.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-8f0000" name="image-8f0000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/f9d37b9/2147483647/strip/true/crop/5359x3008+0+282/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F87%2F63%2Fb47fdbe348b291d1aacfe928fa23%2F186a3186.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a4a82d5/2147483647/strip/true/crop/5359x3008+0+282/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F87%2F63%2Fb47fdbe348b291d1aacfe928fa23%2F186a3186.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a5e0e34/2147483647/strip/true/crop/5359x3008+0+282/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F87%2F63%2Fb47fdbe348b291d1aacfe928fa23%2F186a3186.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Tate McRae performs Sunday on the T-Mobile stage on Day 4 of Lollapalooza. " srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a5e0e34/2147483647/strip/true/crop/5359x3008+0+282/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F87%2F63%2Fb47fdbe348b291d1aacfe928fa23%2F186a3186.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/13d3298/2147483647/strip/true/crop/5359x3008+0+282/resize/980x550!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F87%2F63%2Fb47fdbe348b291d1aacfe928fa23%2F186a3186.jpg 2x" width="490" height="275" data-src="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a5e0e34/2147483647/strip/true/crop/5359x3008+0+282/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F87%2F63%2Fb47fdbe348b291d1aacfe928fa23%2F186a3186.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" > </picture> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Tate McRae performs Sunday on the T-Mobile stage on Day 4 of Lollapalooza.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Anthony Vazquez/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>But for casual viewers getting acquainted with her as a live performer, they may have left disappointed.
